content.title: Timothée Chalamet’s Viral Controversy Sparks A Counter Backlash
content.text: Timothée Chalamet sparked controversy after joking about opera and ballet. (Photo by Dia Dipasupil/FilmMagic)FilmMagicTimothée Chalamet’s controversial comments about ballet and opera fueled a lengthy outrage cycle, so excessive that it sparked a counter-backlash on social media.What Did Timothée Chalamet Say About Ballet And Opera?During a “Town Hall” hosted by Variety and CNN, Timothée Chalamet and Matthew McConaughey discussed the changing landscape of the film industry. Responding to McConaughey’s concerns about short-form video lowering audience attention spans, Chalamet said that he understands that “some people want to be entertained and quickly.”Chalamet reckoned that the film industry is in a healthier state than ballet and opera, delivering his now-infamous quote:“I don’t want to be working in ballet or opera, or things where it’s like, ‘Hey, keep this thing alive.’ Even though it’s like, no one cares about this anymore.” The Marty Supreme star seemed to realize his jab might have offended some viewers, and cheekily added:“All respect to the ballet and opera people out there. I just lost 14 cents in viewership.”Timothée Chalamet’s Quote Sparked BacklashWhile it seemed a forgettable throwaway comment, Chalamet’s quote went viral, attracting backlash from some of the biggest names in ballet and opera.Several opera houses posted rebukes to Chalamet on social media—some even invited the Dune star to attend a show, and see what all the fuss is all about.Multiple celebrities have chimed in on the controversy—so far, Chalamet has been rebuked by Whoopi Goldberg and Nathan Lane on The View, Juliette Binoche, Jamie Lee Curtis, and ballet star Misty Copeland.Opera legend Andrea Bocelli said he was “surprised” by Chalamet’s words, and gave a passionate defense of ballet and opera.“Opera and ballet are art forms that have crossed centuries and continue to speak to the human heart, because they answer a deep need for beauty, truth, and emotion,” Bocelli said.“They are not arts of the past, but living languages that can still move us, make us reflect, and bring different generations together.”It should be noted that Chalamet’s mother and sister both danced with the School of American Ballet. Chalamet has yet to comment on the controversy, but his original statement did not actually dismiss ballet and opera as art forms.However, the flow of defensive posts, articles and quotes were so frequent that social media users pushed back, shocked that Chalamet’s lighthearted comment could spark such a reaction.On X (formerly Twitter), one commentator wrote:“He made an off-color joke and everyone is taking it so seriously. This is why celebrities stick to boring, media-trained answers to everything now.”The response even convinced some commentators that Chalamet was correct, and had struck a nerve.Amusingly, Doja Cat initially took to TikTok to slam Chalamet for his comments, only to delete her fiery, expletive-filled video and post another TikTok backing down, clarifying that she knows “nothing about opera” or ballet.In an unusually candid move from a celebrity, Doja admitted that she was “virtue signaling” and said that she was using the controversy as “something that I could leverage in order for people to connect with me.” “It’s easy,” Doja continued. “It’s a modern way to garner clicks, likes, approval and all kinds of things like that from people.”As the discourse train continued at full steam, some cracked jokes about the painfully prolonged controversy.In an opinion piece defending opera as an art form, Opera Australia CEO Alex Budd described Chalamet’s comment as “quite the achievement.”Budd explained that a “single sentence” from Chalamet “managed to do what our marketing team spends weeks trying to achieve: getting the world talking about opera.”While the ballet and opera world rushed to respond to his words, Chalamet didn’t appear to be stressed out, despite gloomy predictions about his chances at winning an Oscar this weekend.Whatever you think of Chalamet’s words, the controversy makes one thing clear—the Marty Supreme star has reached a dizzying level of fame, in which a single comment can fuel an entire discourse cycle.MORE FROM FORBESForbesTimothée Chalamet’s Viral Zoom Call For ‘Marty Supreme,’ ExplainedBy Dani Di PlacidoForbes‘A Knight Of The Seven Kingdoms’ Shows The True Horror Of KnighthoodBy Dani Di PlacidoForbesEverything You Need To Know About The ‘Backrooms’ MovieBy Dani Di PlacidoForbesTikTok Thinks Timothée Chalamet Is Secretly A U.K. RapperBy Dani Di Placido
